purpose: Curated, high-value open-source skills and upstream references approved for SDR work. This supplements skill-sources.json and is intentionally smaller and more opinionated.

sources.name: n8n
sources.notes: This is the preferred automation/orchestration platform for this project. Community workflow catalogs are discovery only; upstream n8n behavior wins.

sources.name: SearXNG
sources.notes: Never assume the instance is healthy. Check /healthz and a JSON search request before relying on it. Treat empty results caused by upstream engine failures as an error, not evidence that nothing exists.

sources.name: Firecrawl
sources.notes: Use after discovery when clean page/site extraction is needed. Preserve source URLs and evidence provenance.

sources.name: Browser Use
sources.notes: Use only when deterministic HTTP/Firecrawl/Playwright paths are insufficient. Do not expose authenticated sessions or production credentials without explicit need and safeguards.

sources.name: Reacher
sources.notes: Default reference for inexpensive first-pass verification. Ambiguous/risky/unknown results should use the project's paid verifier rules (MillionVerifier) when confidence is required. Review current licensing and SMTP/network constraints before self-hosted production use.

sources.name: OpenAI Cookbook
sources.notes: Use for OpenAI-specific implementation patterns together with current official API documentation.

sources.name: Dify
sources.notes: Reference when a dedicated AI application/workflow platform is justified. Do not add it when existing code or n8n is simpler.

sources.name: LiteLLM
sources.notes: Use only when multi-provider routing, centralized keys, quotas, or model abstraction materially helps.

sources.name: Langfuse
sources.notes: Use when AI/agent behavior reaches production complexity where traces and evaluations are worth operating.

sources.name: NocoDB
sources.notes: May provide an internal UI over operational data, but HubSpot remains the CRM system of record. Review current licensing before adoption.

sources.name: Windmill
sources.notes: Use for code-heavy internal operations when it is materially better than the existing n8n + application path. It is not the default orchestration platform.

sources.name: Listmonk
sources.notes: Reference only. It does not replace SmartLead production sending without a dedicated deliverability pilot.

sources.name: Mautic
sources.notes: Reference only. Do not introduce it simply to duplicate existing n8n/SmartLead/HubSpot behavior.

sources.name: Quickly
sources.notes: Experimental reference only. Never migrate production sending from SmartLead based on feature parity alone; require a controlled deliverability pilot and rollback plan.
